hypothesis: If Darwin is right, the glacial/cold phases of the Pleistocene are recorded at the same times in widely separated regions, so independent records from different ocean basins and latitudes share synchronous cold-stage timing and the global ice-volume/temperature proxy shows long cold intervals.
pass_criterion: In the LR04 benthic d18O stack (Appendix 1), over the last 2.6 Myr at least 80% of the time is spent in glacial-state values (d18O above the series median) in extended intervals of at least 10 kyr, and the glacial maxima (MIS 2, 6, 8, 10, 12) are clearly present, with the stack's inter-site agreement recorded by the authors being high: the per-sample standard error is below 25% of the glacial-interglacial amplitude (about 1.5 per mil) for at least 90% of samples in the last 800 kyr. Together this shows long, globally coherent cold phases with a lower global temperature and larger ice volume at the same times.
fail_criterion: The claim is refuted if the stack shows no sustained high-d18O (cold, ice-volume) intervals of at least 10 kyr within the last 2.6 Myr, or if the stack's standard error exceeds 50% of the glacial-interglacial amplitude (about 1.5 per mil) for more than 30% of the samples in the last 800 kyr. That would mean the contributing records do not agree on timing and no coherent global signal exists.
interpretation: Darwin's "Glacial period" is read as the Pleistocene glacial stages (marine isotope stages). "Simultaneous across the whole world" is read as synchrony within the age-model resolution of globally distributed records (several kyr), not exact contemporaneity. "Global temperature lower" is read through benthic d18O, which mixes deep-water temperature and continental ice volume. This is a modern reinterpretation and a limitation: the stack is an averaged product, so it supports global coherence but cannot show the pole-to-pole belt structure Darwin mentions. It also gives no test of regional leads and lags, which would need the individual core records.

dataset.name: Pliocene-Pleistocene stack of globally distributed benthic stable oxygen isotope records
dataset.why_it_fits: Landing page verified. It offers a ZIP of tab-delimited files: the benthic d18O stack (Appendix 1: age, d18O, standard error), sedimentation rates (Appendix 2) and age-model conversions (Appendix 3). The fields age, d18O and standard error are used to measure the duration of glacial intervals and the coherence of the globally distributed records.
